title: interaction-snapshot-prd-sketch
content:
Purpose / one-liner:
A lightweight, first-class "interaction snapshot" primitive that lets apps capture a compact representation of an in-progress user interaction for fast resume, cheaper rehydration, and smarter routing. Target is developer-facing API + small UX primitives in the console.

Context / motivation (notes to self):
- Lots of product teams want a 'save and resume' experience without paying full token cost to reconstruct context.
- Current options: store full messages (expensive) or ad-hoc summarization on client side (fragile, inconsistent).
- A snapshot primitive can be optimized for storage, retrieval latency, and downstream inference costs (embedding + retrieval, or partial KV rehydrate).
- Must treat privacy/PII/risk as first-class: snapshots often contain user data.

Hypothesis:
If we provide a snapshot API that stores an immutable, versioned compact summary + optional structured metadata and embeddings, teams will use it to reduce avg tokens per resumed session by >=40% and reduce latency for conversation rehydration by >=30%.

Persona(s):
- Product engineer at SMB building a chat agent: wants cheap resume across devices.
- Platform engineer at enterprise: wants snapshots to be auditable, TTL-controlled, and KMS-encrypted.
- End-user: expects fast continuity when switching devices or returning to a conversation.

Core user stories (rough):
- As a developer, I can call POST /v1/snapshots with conversation_id and optional "strategy" to create a compact snapshot that returns snapshot_id and size_estimate.
- As a developer, I can GET /v1/snapshots/:id to retrieve the snapshot and optionally request a full rehydrate payload vs. lightweight metadata.
- As a developer, I can attach policies: retention_ttl, encrypt_with_customer_kms, allow_tool_calls_on_restore=false.
- As an end-user, when I reopen a conversation, the client requests snapshot_id and the server rehydrates into the chat UI with a human-readable summary (and a link to view full history) within 150ms.

Snapshot shape (brainstorm):
- header: snapshot_id, created_by, model_hint, version
- metadata: user_labels, flags (sensitive, embeddable), last_turn_ts
- compact_summary: short (<=256 tokens) abstractive summary optimized for rehydration
- sketch: a small sequence of canonical turns (1-3 turns) preserved verbatim when marked necessary
- embeddings: 1-3 vectors for retrieval / ranking
- provenance: list of tickets/feature ids that triggered this snapshot
- storage hints: shard_key, ttl_seconds

Storage/encoding ideas:
- Store snapshots as compressed JSONL-like blobs (gzip) with an index for fast fetch.
- Two-tier storage: hot cache (fast rehydrate) for recent snapshots, cold blobstore for older TTLed ones.
- Optional on-device encrypted snapshot for end-to-end scenarios (customer-managed key) — heavy lift but requested by regulated customers.

API design considerations (quick):
- POST /v1/snapshots
  - body: { conversation_id, created_by, strategy: [auto, user-save, periodic], max_summary_tokens, preserve_turns: N }
  - response: { snapshot_id, size_bytes, embeddings_present, created_at }
- GET /v1/snapshots/:id?level=[summary|minimal|full]
  - level=minimal returns only metadata + vector ids; summary returns compact_summary; full returns sketch + provenance.
- PATCH /v1/snapshots/:id to add tags/labels or escalate sensitivity flag. Immutable payload but mutable metadata.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API that creates and reads snapshot objects with metadata and compact_summary.
- Snapshot create latency < 200ms median for small inputs (summary generation moved to async but with sync quick path).
- Retrieval latency from hot cache < 150ms p50.
- Embedding vector (if requested) computed and stored and indexable in our vector store.
- Basic audit log entries for snapshot create/read with user id + IP.

Metrics to validate success:
- avg_tokens_per_resume (control vs snapshots)
- resume_success_rate (user continues after resume within 30s)
- snapshot_create_latency and snapshot_read_latency
- snapshot_storage_cost_per_1k_sessions

Rollout plan / experiment:
- Phase 0: internal feature flag + sample SDK endpoint for teams building prototypes. Collect feedback.
- Phase 1: B2B beta with optional KMS encryption and longer TTL. Run small cohort (5 customers), track token savings and UX metrics.
- Phase 2: GA for hosted API, with console UI for browsing snapshots, TTL controls, and audit exports.

Security & privacy checklist (must):
- default retention 30 days, adjustable per-customer (enterprise can set policy)
- snapshot-level encryption at rest; customer KMS optional
- PII redaction helpers: built-in redaction pass on create (configurable), flag 'sensitive' to block embeddings
- redact/obfuscate before snapshots are used to warm model prompts for LLM if flagged sensitive

Open questions / tradeoffs (todo):
- Should snapshots be mutable? (Pro: fix mistakes; Con: complicates auditability). Lean immutable payload + mutable metadata.
- Who pays for embedding storage? Per-request charged or monthly index fee? Need pricing discussion with finance.
- How to format snapshot for multi-turn tool-enabled conversations (tool outputs often large)? Might need tool-output references instead of inlined.

Prototype notes / dev tasks (rough):
- quick prototype: SDK helper that runs a short summarization prompt + embeds it -> store in vector index and create snapshot record. (owner: Ethan)
- console: snapshot browser table + preview panel, TTL set control, delete button (owner: Talia)
- infra: hot cache layer for recent snapshots; retention sweeper job (owner: infra)
- tests: CR/QA for PII-redaction and KMS encryption flow

Edge cases / gotchas:
- Snapshot of a streaming conversation where last turn is partial — need explicit commit event from client.
- Older snapshots created on different model version — rehydrate should surface model_hint and optionally re-run summary using current model.
- Snapshot expansion attacks: attacker submits snapshot with huge preserved_turns; must enforce server-side limits.

UX micro-copy ideas for client:
- "Saved snapshot: we’ll use a short summary to resume your session quickly. View full history"
- On restore: show a gray bar: "Resumed from snapshot taken at 2026-02-02 — some details omitted to keep things fast."

Next steps (checklist):
- [ ] Wireframe snapshot console panel
- [ ] Draft API schema + error codes
- [ ] Spike: decide sync vs async summary pipeline cost/latency tradeoffs
- [ ] Legal consult: retention defaults for EU customers
- [ ] Pricing note to finance (token savings model)

Notes to self: keep MVP tiny and opt-in. Focus on clear developer ergonomics (simple POST/GET, explicit flags). Avoid trying to solve full on-device KMS in MVP.

Related threads / context links:
- Notes from product sync 2026-01-10 (see GH-PR-418)
- Slack thread: #resume-ux (linked above)

Scratch brainstorming bits (random):
- "micro-snapshot" that only stores last 2 user turns + intent label — smallest possible resume
- Offer 'snapshot hints' API to allow client to annotate which turns are important (developer responsibility)
- Consider 'deltas' so we can cheaply compute diffs between snapshots for storage optimization

End of notes.
